title: OpenQC Algorithm Entry
description: Schema for algorithm.json files in openqc algorithm repos. Each algorithm repo must have a valid algorithm.json at its root.

slug.description: URL-safe unique identifier. Must match the repo name suffix (algo-{slug}).

author.description: GitHub username or organization that maintains this algorithm.

description.description: Brief description of the algorithm (1-2 sentences).

industries.description: Industry/domain tags. Must match values in TAXONOMY.json. Examples: education, finance, chemistry, optimization, cryptography, logistics, pharma, materials, ml, energy.

techniques.description: Quantum computing technique tags. Must match values in TAXONOMY.json. Examples: gate, vqa, annealing, qec, analog, classical.

difficulty.description: Difficulty level for the target user.

algorithm_type.description: Execution type — determines job routing and result format.

qubit_count.description: Number of qubits (or problem variables for annealing/classical).

min_qubits.description: Minimum qubits needed. For scalable algorithms, this is the smallest useful size.

recommended_backends.description: Suggested simulator profiles. Examples: vortex-noiseless, vortex-ibm-heron-like.

access.description: Access tier. open = full code in repo. gated = metadata only, request access. paid = metadata only, pay to run.

access_reason.description: Why this algorithm is gated/paid (shown to users requesting access).

trial_runs.description: Number of free trial runs before payment required.

source.description: Whether this algorithm is maintained by the openqc team or a community contributor.

circuit_qasm.description: QASM 2.0 circuit source code. Omitted for paid/gated algorithms.

template_code.description: Python source for build() + interpret(). Omitted for paid/gated algorithms.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema for algorithm input parameters.

category.description: Legacy category field (for backward compat with existing JSON files).

blockers.description: Dependencies preventing materialization. Used with status: coming-soon.
